passage:
On a rainy day, art teacher Ms. Lin asked her students to paint without brushes. She gave them paper, watercolor, and plastic trays.
Students put drops of color on the paper and placed the paper outside for ten seconds. Rain hit the colors and moved them in surprising ways.
Some pictures looked like flowers. Others looked like rivers or fireworks. No two paintings were the same.
A student said, "But we did not control everything."
Ms. Lin answered, "That is why they are interesting."
The class learned that art is not always about making the world obey your plan. Sometimes it is about working with what happens and finding beauty in the result.
